Early voting is pretty robust, where six days out and almost 40 million people have voted,
and that's climbing. But it would be folly to read too much into early voting.
Republicans overwhelmingly vote on election day in person, so that's a big wildcard here.
In the states that do report early votes by party, so far the split is 44% Democratic to 31%
Republican. That may sound like a big Democratic advantage, but even in a year when they lost

was over $50,000. Willa Rubin, NPR News. This is NPR News. A federal judge says the
Justice Department's request to stop California from processing the ballots of up to 20,000
people would, in his words, wreak havoc on midterm voting. The judge rejected the DOJ's
request Wednesday. The Justice Department had alleged that the people on its list were likely
non-citizens. But state officials say that list is unreliable and the Justice Department made a

become more complicated as AI becomes part of everyday work. An employer has to accommodate
religion except if it leads to substantial increased cost in the overall business.
Depending on what those costs look like and depending on kind of the role that AI plays,
